overall: The AG found the Wakefield Town Council did not violate the Open Meeting Law: the four September 8 notice topics were sufficiently specific or were not discussed, and the July 14 allegation was untimely.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged notice topic 6B (Town Meeting Warrant Articles review) should have referenced a proposed Town Charter amendment limiting warrant article debate.
allegations.key_passage: Although the detail proposed by the complainant might have been beneficial, the topic as drafted was sufficiently specific.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged notice topic 6C (Town Council Policy Review: Public Participation) was insufficiently specific.
allegations.key_passage: A member of the public reasonably could understand from topic 6C in the notice that the Council might discuss a review of the policy concerning public participation, a phrase often used to denote public comment.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged topic 7B (200 Quannapowitt Parkway grading request) failed to name the adjacent town-owned property where grading would extend.
allegations.key_passage: Although a close question, we find the notice to be sufficiently specific as to this topic.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged topic 7D (Water Street deed) was insufficient because the parcel number listed does not exist.
allegations.key_passage: Because topic 7D was not discussed at the September 8 meeting, we find no violation as to this allegation.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the July 14 meeting notice was not sufficiently specific, but was filed more than 30 days after the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: The allegation concerning the July 14 meeting, raised in the September 7 complaint, was untimely.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
